prompt: A recipe uses $2$ cups of flour to make $24$ cookies. At the same rate, how many cups of flour are needed to make $60$ cookies?
hint: Set up a proportion with cups on top and cookies on the bottom in both fractions.

hints.text: Set up a proportion with cups on top and cookies on the bottom in both fractions.

learningObjective: Set up and solve a proportion in context.
explanation: Keep the units consistent: $\dfrac{2 \text{ cups}}{24 \text{ cookies}} = \dfrac{c \text{ cups}}{60 \text{ cookies}}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Find the rate per cookie first
steps: $2$ cups makes $24$ cookies, so one cookie takes $\dfrac{2}{24} = \dfrac{1}{12}$ cup.
The unit-rate route takes one extra step but reads more naturally, and it makes the answer easy to sanity-check.
